sanitization: Real Devin CLI 3000.10.31 hook stdin captured via a capture-only .devin/hooks.v1.json logger (plus a .claude/settings.json SubagentStop probe — see C16) on Linux/WSL2. Only paths, session/prompt/tool-use/agent identifiers, shell ids, and verbose prompt text were replaced with placeholders. Property names, nesting, booleans, missing-vs-null distinctions, response status, correlation relationships, and EVENT ORDER (one global sequence, including interleaved parent/child events) are preserved exactly. Agent-authored report and stop text is kept verbatim where it is load-bearing evidence (it quotes only fixture file contents). No secrets, no real document content, no unredacted user prompts.

fieldObservations: C11 ANSWERED: a parent Stop DOES fire while a background subagent is still in-flight. Order: launch PostToolUse → child glob Pre/Post → PARENT Stop ('launched') → child read Pre/Post → CHILD Stop (the sentinel report) → PARENT Stop #2 ('The background subagent finished…') → SessionEnd. The 3000.10.21 changelog note ('the turn stays active until it finishes') does NOT suppress the Stop hook — the pending-subagent carve-out is LOAD-BEARING.

Attribution: the 7th event is the PARENT's Stop (its message is the instructed reply 'launched'); the 10th is the CHILD's Stop (its message is the child's sentinel report); the 11th is the PARENT's second Stop on the post-notification turn. Stop payloads carry NO field identifying which agent stopped — attribution is only possible from last_assistant_message content and ordering.

A SECOND parent Stop fires after the <subagent_completion_notification> is delivered to the agent's context — under the SAME session_id AND the SAME prompt_id (the notification turn does not rotate prompt_id; only real user prompts do). A session can therefore emit multiple Stop events per prompt_id.

A background child's Stop can also arrive BETWEEN two of the parent's own events (here between parent Stop #1 and parent Stop #2); a Stop payload is never attributable to parent-vs-child by any structured field.
No SubagentStop event fired anywhere in the sequence (see C16 — the key is not loadable).

fieldObservations: A background child's approval-gated tool is AUTO-DENIED: the exec fires PreToolUse ONLY ('curl -sI https://example.com') with NO PostToolUse — the same hook signature as a rejected tool call.

Despite the denial the blocked read_subagent returns success:true with the SAME output as a successful terminal read ('Subagent <agent-id> completed. Its full report is delivered…') — a denied/failed child reads back as 'completed'. The binary's 'Subagent <id> exited with an error' read string did NOT appear for this failure mode.

The failure is visible ONLY in the CHILD's Stop last_assistant_message ('…denied because this agent is running in the background, and tools requiring approval are automatically denied in that mode…'), which lands inside the parent's blocked read_subagent window (between its PreToolUse and PostToolUse).

Implication for the classifier: read_subagent 'completed' output CANNOT distinguish a clean completion from a child that failed internally — and there is no hook-visible PostToolUse for the denied exec to correlate against.
The parent's own Stop ('The subagent's curl command was denied…') follows the read_subagent PostToolUse; SessionEnd keeps reason='other'.

fieldObservations: NEW field on 3000.10.31: run_subagent tool_input.resume takes an agent_id STRING ('resume':'<agent-id>') to re-dispatch a COMPLETED agent. The resumed call has NO is_background field — resumes always run in the FOREGROUND (matches subagents.mdx).

The resumed dispatch gets a NEW tool_use_id but its completion output embeds the SAME agent_id ('Subagent agent_id=<agent-id> completed successfully:'). One agent_id can have multiple launch/terminal cycles — agent_id alone is NOT unique per lifecycle.

Between the resume PreToolUse and PostToolUse, the resumed child's tool calls (read, edit) and its Stop enter the parent hook stream exactly as a fresh foreground dispatch — sharing session_id+prompt_id, no identity fields.

In a FOREGROUND dispatch the child's Stop lands BEFORE the parent's run_subagent PostToolUse (both cycles observed: Stop 'Created …a.txt' precedes the completion PostToolUse; resumed Stop 'Appended "beta"…' precedes the resume PostToolUse).
No new structured identity fields appeared anywhere: still no agent_id/agent_type/profile on child tool events or Stops.

C16_subagentStopNegative.scenario: SubagentStop registered as a hook event key. It could NOT be registered in .devin/hooks.v1.json (an entry there makes the CLI log 'unknown variant `SubagentStop`' and reject the WHOLE file — hooks discovery loaded=0, zero capture files, CLI still exits 0); it was registered in .claude/settings.json instead, where the same warning skips only that file while the devin provider still loads (loaded=7, by_provider=[devin=7]).
fieldObservations: NEGATIVE PROVEN: no SubagentStop event is dispatched on 3000.10.31 — no *SubagentStop* capture file exists in any run, and no run produced a startup error (every run exited 0).

SubagentStop is NOT a loadable event key in EITHER config location. In hooks.v1.json it poisons the entire file (WARN 'Failed to parse hooks file … unknown variant `SubagentStop`', loaded=0 — all 7 real events lose their hooks). In .claude/settings.json the same unknown-variant warning rejects that file alone ('Failed to parse JSONC … unknown variant `SubagentStop`').
Unknown event keys are a per-FILE rejection (WARN only), never a startup failure.

SubagentStop exists in the binary only as a ClaudeHookSpecificOutput OUTPUT variant (accepted in hookSpecificOutput.hookEventName) — never as a dispatched event. A SubagentStop-shaped payload remains an adapter-side construction (as the Copilot adapter synthesizes), not a host-observable event.
